solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush died beside tree

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off after a death, leaving the scene beside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to hurry or move quickly, a straightforward synonym of rush as a verb.

clue.text: Help over ethnic group in critical attack

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals that the word aid is turned back to front

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: Offering help to an ethnic group in the middle of a fierce criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the word is written upwards, so it reads backwards on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter, forceful verbal assault on someone or something, a harsh denunciation.

clue.text: Highly inclined to soak

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to leave something immersed in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a sharp gradient and a verb for leaving something to soak in liquid.

clue.text: How pupils end up dead cute with exercise

indicators.note: exercise suggests the letters are put through their paces and rearranged

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren finish their schooling looking terribly sweet thanks to some workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DEAD CUTE are rearranged to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils who have been through school finish up schooled and taught, which is the state the definition describes.

clue.text: Very bright 24-hours — see about golf?

indicators.note: about read as on or concerning, so the see word is placed on the golf letter, following it

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a whole day is enough to watch golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the loose part: it does not wrap anything, but reads as 'on the subject of', so the see word simply follows the golf letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-Glo is a brand of fluorescent paint, so the word describes glaringly vivid colours.

clue.text: Having some friends for dinner?

parts.note: read literally, the friends are the meal rather than the guests

explanation.walkthrough: The innocent phrase for inviting guests is read as eating them.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of eating human flesh, which is what serving your friends as the meal would amount to.

clue.text: Winnings thanks to court cards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
kings are court cards, along with queens and jacks

explanation.surface: Money won at the card table thanks to a hand full of picture cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money taken in, the receipts or proceeds, here likened to what a gambler wins.

clue.text: Please note bird that's passed

parts.note: do as in do sit down, a polite request
do (doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A request to take notice of a bird that has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The first DO is the polite imperative, as in 'do come in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius that became extinct in the seventeenth century, so it has passed away.

clue.text: One of the stone circle sites — Aubrey reconstructed about five

definitions.text: One of the stone circle sites

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged name goes around the numeral
reconstructed means rebuilt in a new form, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The antiquary John Aubrey, who studied stone circles, is jumbled up around a numeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructed' turns AUBREY into AEBURY, and 'about' puts that around V. John Aubrey was the 17th-century antiquary who first recorded the site.
explanation.definitionFit: Avebury in Wiltshire, England, has the largest prehistoric stone ring in Britain, near Stonehenge.

clue.text: Male relative almost spoke without too much muddle

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the relative is dropped

parts.note: an uncle is a male relative
uttered means spoke

explanation.surface: An uncle talks clearly, avoiding confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims UNCLE to UNCL, followed by UTTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncluttered is tidy and free of mess, without a jumble of excess things.

clue.text: Exposed, took a winding path, hiding head

indicators.note: hiding its head means the first letter is concealed and so removed

parts.note: snaked means moved along a twisting course

explanation.surface: Someone stripped bare wanders along a twisting route, keeping their head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding head' drops the S from SNAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means bare or uncovered, so open to view and unprotected.

clue.text: I call parson about troublemaker

indicators.note: about here means around in a jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone telephones the vicar about a local nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I CALL PARSON are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapscallion is a mischievous rascal or rogue who causes bother.

clue.text: Sting is the cryptic outcome of this still

parts.words: Sting is the cryptic outcome of this
parts.note: the answer is split into three chunks, and its middle chunk is read as the word joining the other two, whose joining gives the sting

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter boasting that a stinging remark comes from a riddle, delivered calmly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ST AND ING: putting ST and ING together gives STING, so the clue describes the answer's own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing water is still and unmoving, so the adjective means stationary or stagnant.

clue.text: Seafood soup is confined to British Quebec

indicators.note: confined to means held within, so the little word is shut inside the other letters

parts.note: Que. is an abbreviation for the Canadian province of Quebec

explanation.surface: A seafood dish said to be found only in a British-ruled Quebec.
explanation.definitionFit: A bisque is a rich, creamy soup traditionally made from shellfish such as lobster or crab.

clue.text: Carpets woven in ranges of colours

indicators.note: weaving twists threads together, so the letters of the word are intertwined into a new order

explanation.surface: Rugs made with yarn in a rainbow of shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra is the plural of spectrum, the band of hues into which light splits.

clue.text: British benefit, getting hunting dog

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A British advantage gained by owning a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged breed of hound bred to track hares and rabbits by scent.

clue.text: US state, not a Republican state

indicators.note: not means without, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: Arkansas is a state of the USA

explanation.surface: A political quip that a certain US state does not vote Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'state' is ARKANSAS; 'not' removes A and R, from the front, leaving another state.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a Midwestern state, one of the fifty that make up the United States.

clue.text: What olive oil can be more unused?

parts.note: extra means additional, more
virgin means untouched or not used before

explanation.surface: A question about how fresh olive oil can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra virgin is the top grade of olive oil, from the first cold pressing of the fruit.

clue.text: Blood around small prickly plant

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the blood word encloses the letter

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Blood from scratches on a little thorny bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny evergreen shrub with yellow flowers, common on British heathland; also called furze.

clue.text: Cries noisily over losing large pad

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken out
in a down clue, over means the word is flipped and read upwards

parts.note: bawls means cries loudly
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone sobbing loudly as they lose a big cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BAWLS into SLWAB, and 'losing' removes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a small absorbent wad of cotton or gauze used to clean a wound or take a sample.

clue.text: Conflict about the empty lake's contents

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the conflict word wraps the other letters

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, leaving only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dispute over what fills the emptied lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' hollows out a word, keeping only its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is a body of fresh liquid, so what it holds is the clear liquid that fills rivers and seas.

clue.text: Military type regularly is harmful before unfinished attack

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the second, fourth and so on
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a raid is a surprise attack

explanation.surface: A soldier regularly causes harm before an attack left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of IS HARMFUL, giving SAMU; 'unfinished' cuts RAID to RAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Hold up vessel carrying cereal product

indicators.note: carrying here means bearing on top, so the cereal word rides ahead of the vessel word

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain
a dish is a vessel for food

explanation.surface: A bowl filled with breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' looks like a container signal, but here the cereal simply rides in front of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave something aloft, flourishing a weapon to show it off or threaten.

clue.text: Mountain visible in Khyber, generally

indicators.note: visible in means the letters can be seen within the following words

explanation.surface: A peak that can be seen in the Khyber region, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The Khyber Pass is the mountain route between Afghanistan and Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg is a South African word for a mountain, and also short for iceberg, a floating ice mountain.
